name: Blouin & Steel Fabricators
old_description: We provide complete structural steel fabrication services based out of Northfield, NH.
about:
Blouin Steel Fabricators, Inc. operates from Northfield, New Hampshire, where it has provided structural steel fabrication services since 1995. The company was founded that year and has since built a reputation for handling complete structural steel projects.

The shop fabricates primary structural members as well as miscellaneous items such as stairways, safety bollards, and steel concrete embeds. It also offers custom metal fabrication, miscellaneous steel stair fabrication, and in-house erection crews to complete installations. Steel sales round out the offering for construction and manufacturing needs.

The company serves commercial, residential, and municipal clients. Commercial projects include schools, hospitals, banks, lumber yards, pharmacies, and apartment buildings. Residential work covers renovations, upgrades, repairs, and steel supply. Municipal contracts involve waste water facilities, water treatment plants, and ponds for water management.

Blouin Steel emphasizes meticulous attention to detail on every product, regardless of size, and states that its focus is entirely on client needs and satisfaction. The firm positions itself as a creator of reliable solutions tailored to each project’s requirements.

name: Blue Ridge Furniture
old_description: Transform your space with heirloom quality pieces from Blue Ridge Furniture, the top furniture store in Honey Brook, PA.
about:
Blue Ridge Furniture operates from Honey Brook, Pennsylvania, where it was founded in 1994 by Sidney Burkholder. The family-owned business began as a custom furnishings shop and has remained under Burkholder family stewardship since the early 2000s, with the youngest generation now working in the workshop.

The company manufactures solid-wood furniture for dining rooms, living rooms, bedrooms, offices, and outdoor spaces, along with a signature live-edge table line. Production takes place in a dedicated finishing and hardware-assembly building, while an 11,000-square-foot showroom in nearby Narvon displays the range. Every piece is built from premium hardwoods — oak, cherry, walnut, and maple — with no veneers used.

Customers include homeowners throughout the Mid-Atlantic region (Philadelphia, Lancaster, Wilmington, Baltimore, New York City) and commercial clients such as businesses ordering conference tables. The company also ships finished pieces worldwide.

Blue Ridge Furniture emphasizes its position as the actual manufacturer, offering custom design consultations with rendered drawings for client approval before production, multiple finishing options including stain-color matching, and a white-glove delivery service that handles assembly and placement.

name: Bluepeak
old_description: We’re all about improving connectivity and growing opportunities in the heartland.
about:
Bluepeak is headquartered in Rapid City, South Dakota. The company operates fiber-to-the-home networks across six states: Oklahoma, Wyoming, South Dakota, North Dakota, Texas, and Minnesota. Leadership includes Chief Executive Officer Rich Fish, a telecom veteran with prior roles at AT&T and WOW!, Chief Operating Officer Cash Hagen, a U.S. Marine Corps veteran, Chief Commercial Officer Lana Frank, Chief Business Development Officer Mike Harry, Vice President of Human Resources Mary Armstrong, and General Counsel Marc Krasney. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

Bluepeak builds and operates a fiber-to-the-home network delivering symmetrical speeds up to 5 Gbps for residential customers and up to 10 Gbps for businesses. The company offers tiered internet plans starting at 300 Mbps, with included eero Secure Wi-Fi and modem on higher tiers, plus professional installation. It also provides television services through a traditional channel lineup (Bluepeak TV) and an app-based streaming platform (Bluepeak Stream). As of the latest figures, the network connects over 275,000 homes. A dedicated New Construction division handles ongoing fiber expansion.

The company serves both residential and business customers in its six-state footprint. Residential users include households streaming, gaming, and working remotely, while business customers range from small offices to enterprise accounts requiring high-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity. Bluepeak positions its service for applications such as telehealth, online learning, and remote work.

Bluepeak emphasizes community investment beyond infrastructure, citing a commitment to "connect people and create access and opportunity where there wasn't any before." The company is Great Place to Work® Certified and highlights local, regional support call centers as a differentiator. Its stated mission is to deliver "unexpectedly fast internet, affordably priced, locally rooted."

about:
Bolen's Control House operates from Boise, Idaho, where it has established itself as a supplier of industrial automation components and a UL508A-certified panel shop. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The business stocks and sells control products from lines such as Siemens SIRIUS, WAGO terminal blocks, Rittal enclosures, Schneider Harmony push buttons, and Omron automation solutions. In its panel shop, the company builds open and enclosed industrial control panels, performs device mounting, DIN-rail assemblies, harness and sensor terminations, and custom cable assemblies. Three full-time application engineers with a combined 50-plus years of experience support design, engineering, and integration services, and the shop also provides CAD drawings for panel layouts and schematics.

The company's bin-stocking and blanket-contract programs are geared toward operations that need predictable inventory flow, while its same-day shipping pledge serves urgent replacement needs.

Bolen's Control House emphasizes its UL508A panel shop authorization, same-day shipment for orders placed before 2:00 PM Mountain Time, and the depth of its application-engineering staff as core differentiators. The firm also offers customer part-number cross-referencing, specialized packaging, and on-site training seminars to reduce integration effort for its buyers.

about:
Boom Island Woodworking operates from the Northeast Minneapolis Arts District in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2019 by Eddie Phillips, a mechanical engineer with a minor in product design, who initially restarted woodworking as a creative outlet. After building a brand and customer base, Phillips left the corporate world in 2022 to pursue furniture making full time.

The shop produces fine furniture, custom designs, and functional wood art using sustainably sourced hardwoods and traditional joinery techniques. Each piece is built as a one-of-a-kind commission or a signature design, emphasizing heirloom-quality construction meant to last generations.

The primary customers are residential clients seeking custom furniture for their homes — dining tables, beds, and other pieces that anchor living spaces. The custom process is collaborative, guiding clients from concept through wood species selection, dimensions, finishes, and design details. Regular email updates keep clients informed throughout the build.

Phillips describes a philosophy rooted in craftsmanship, authenticity, and a deep connection to materials. The goal is to create objects that carry timeless beauty and evoke emotion, going beyond mere utility to become lasting pieces of functional art.

about:
Border States’ Chicago branch operates from a facility on West Ferdinand Street in Chicago, Illinois. The company has served construction, industrial, and utility markets for more than 70 years and is structured as a 100 % employee‑owned enterprise. No founding year or individual founders are disclosed in the available materials.

The branch functions as a full‑service distributor and solutions provider. Its offerings span back‑office and financial streamlining, building information modeling (BIM), equipment maintenance and testing, customized kitting, prefabricated modular switchboard and panel assembly, material management, project management, Rockwell Automation repair and remanufacturing, on‑site staffing and advanced logistics (4PL/5PL), technical advisory and assessments, training in automation and natural gas, utility metering (AMR/AMI), and customized wire and cable services. The company does not publish facility square footage, headcount, or annual volume figures.

Primary customers are contractors, industrial plants, and utility operators in the construction, industrial, and utility sectors. The quality blog illustrates how crews rely on the distributor for guy‑wire anchors used in transmission and cell‑tower installations. The company’s “by industry leaders” list references supplier brands such as 3M, Lithonia Lighting, Leviton, Encore Wire, Southwire, and Prysmian Group, indicating the product lines it carries for those markets.

Border States emphasizes its employee‑ownership model as a differentiator, stating that dedicated owners are invested in customer success. The company pledges accountability, expertise, relationship‑based collaboration, flexibility, and transparency, aiming to treat each client’s business as its own.

about:
Brian Hubel operates Hubel Handcrafted Interiors Inc. from Colorado Springs, Colorado. The business, founded by Brian A. Hubel, builds custom furniture one piece at a time and also offers woodworking classes and shop services to other woodworkers.

The shop produces handmade tables, seating, storage, lighting, clocks, shelving, and wall art, each designed and fabricated by Hubel himself. about:
Bridon American Corporation operates from Exeter, Pennsylvania, as the U.S. arm of Bekaert's rope division. Bekaert, a global leader in steel wire transformation and coating technologies, traces its rope-making heritage back more than 300 years, while the modern corporation builds on over 140 years of innovation in materials and manufacturing. The business brings together centuries of rope-making expertise with Bekaert's strengths in technology and innovation to serve mission-critical applications worldwide.

The company manufactures precision-engineered steel wire ropes and synthetic ropes under the Bridon® and Bexco® brands. Its product portfolio covers mooring, towing, lifting, and hauling ropes for heavy-duty use. Beyond manufacturing, Bridon American provides Ropes360® services, including installation of reels up to 450 metric tons with on-site splicing and socketing, visual and advanced non-destructive inspections, forensic laboratory testing of new and retired ropes, repair and maintenance such as re-lubrication and re-socketing, training, and custom design with tailored logistics and consignment stocking.

Customers span renewable energy, oil and gas, mining, cranes and industrial, and commercial fishing. In renewable energy, the ropes are used on wind turbine installation vessels. Oil and gas clients rely on them for offshore drilling, marine riser tensioners, and offshore lifting. Mining operations use shovel ropes, dragline ropes, and drum winder ropes. Crane applications include offshore cranes, telescopic mobile cranes, and industrial hoist ropes. Commercial fishing fleets employ trawl warps and purse wires.

Bekaert positions its rope business around four legacy strengths: heritage in mission-critical rope manufacturing, technology leadership and innovation, deep understanding of market needs, and global presence with local expertise. The company emphasizes a "better together" approach, co-creating solutions with customers to extend rope life, maximize safety, and reduce downtime through integrated inspection, testing, and maintenance services.

name: Bryce Corporation Warehouse
old_description: We use cookies and analytics tools to understand how our site is used and to improve your experience. We don't sell your personal information. By continuing to use this site, you agree to our use of cookies.
about:
The company traces its origins to 1922 when William H. Bryce Sr. developed waxing technology at the Dixie Company in Dallas, Texas. He founded Dixie Wax Paper in Memphis in 1927, and in 1969 William H. Bryce Jr. established Bryce Corporation to convert polypropylene films for the snack food market. The business remains family-owned and operated, now in its fourth generation under Chairman and CEO Thomas J. Bryce, who took the helm in 1997, alongside his sons-in-law Sean Bowie and Stephen Perkins.

The company specializes in film conversion and flexible packaging production, offering flexographic printing, lamination, slitting, perforation, pouch making, and logistics. Through affiliate Cyber Graphics it provides design, prepress, and plate-making services, while minority-owned partner Johnson Bryce adds waxing and coating capabilities. Facilities in the Southeast support large-volume runs with automated quality systems including statistical process control, 100% web detection, and a closed-loop quality system. The operation is Safe Quality Food (SQF) certified.

Bryce serves the food, snack, pet care, household, and health and beauty sectors, with specific markets including salty snacks, confectionery, pet food, bakery, frozen foods, and personal care. Its packaging protects products for nationally recognized brands across these categories.

Founded on a legacy of technological innovation — from pioneering polypropylene film conversion to extended-gamut flexographic printing — the company emphasizes sustainable packaging solutions, generational commitment to employees and community, and responsiveness through its affiliate network.

name: Buck Mason Knitting Mills
old_description: One brisk Saturday in October, I received a call at my home in Pennsylvania from my friend Joe. He was talking anxiously about a shirt factory in Mohnton that had just closed its doors after 100 years. "They’re sending the entire team home next Friday,” Joe explained. “Erik, these folks know how to make t-shirts. It’s in the water out there. Would you and Sasha have any interest in buying the place?”
about:
Buck Mason Knitting Mills operates in Mohnton, Pennsylvania, a town with a century-long tradition of shirt manufacturing. After the sudden closure of a factory that had run continuously for 100 years, Buck Mason co-founders Erik and Sasha acquired the facility and rehired its workforce, restarting production within months.

The mill houses knitting machines that enable the company to develop proprietary fabrics from raw yarn, alongside sewing equipment for garment assembly. The operation focuses on t-shirt production, with the capability to control fabric development from scratch.

The company serves the apparel and textile manufacturing sectors, primarily producing for its own Buck Mason brand.

The acquisition was driven by a desire to vertically integrate Buck Mason's supply chain, revive domestic manufacturing, and preserve the skilled workforce of Mohnton. The founders viewed the existing factory as a sound business opportunity and a chance to rebuild a piece of American industrial heritage.

name: Burnette Foods, Inc.
old_description: All the flavor, color, and texture expected in a well-established, quality brand.
about:
Burnette Foods, Inc. is a third-generation, family-owned food manufacturer headquartered in New Era, Michigan. The company traces its roots to 1935, when Mae and Theodore Sherman purchased a cherry orchard in Central Lake, Michigan, leveraging the region’s sandy soil and Lake Michigan climate. Their son William and his wife Marian later established Sherman Canning Company in East Jordan in 1961, formalizing the family’s entry into food processing. Today, the business operates as Burnette Foods, with production facilities across Michigan.

The company specializes in shelf-stable fruit and vegetable products, including canned dry-pack beans, applesauce, fruit fillings, pumpkin, hummus, fruit cups, meat items, salads, and fruit juices. State-of-the-art processing facilities handle canning, packaging, and private-label production for national and regional brands.

Burnette Foods serves private-label customers, grocery retailers, and food-service distributors seeking a single source for a wide variety of shelf-stable items. Its customer base includes brands that place their own labels on the company’s products, as well as distributors stocking shelves and kitchens nationwide. The company emphasizes long-standing corporate relationships built through experienced sales and customer-service teams.

Burnette Foods differentiates itself through integrity, innovation, and forward-thinking practices. Its processing aims to retain the flavor, color, texture, and nutrient integrity of fruits and vegetables. Sustainability initiatives include water and energy reduction, recycling of corrugated and tin packaging, upcycling fruit pits, and converting by-products into livestock feed.

name: C & O Manufacturing - Custom Metal Fabricator
old_description: is the name of the game in the display industry, and we have created some of the most unique, awe-inspiring, winning, and yes, strange displays you can imagine.
about:
C & O Manufacturing was founded in 1995 by Cesar and Oscar in a cramped storage-like shop in Irwindale, California. The two founders worked 16-hour days cutting, rolling, bending, and welding steel, building a reputation through word-of-mouth without advertising. Now headquartered in Pico Rivera, California, the company operates as a family-owned business where the founding philosophy of hands-on craftsmanship continues to guide operations.

The company provides custom display fabrication, metal fabrication, laser cutting, and custom industrial parts from a facility exceeding 32,000 square feet. Its shop includes 14 welding stations staffed entirely by skilled craftsmen—no robots—and offers in-house capabilities spanning cutting, rolling, bending, welding, laser etching, powder coating, chrome plating, painting, assembly, and packaging. C & O also produces wood and acrylic displays, combining metal with wood, plastic, glass, and other materials to create countertop displays, floor displays, and trade-show componentry.

C & O serves industries including beauty, hospitality, retail, exhibit, casino, and hotel sectors, as well as industrial clients needing custom machine parts. Its portfolio includes display work for Las Vegas casinos and hotels such as Hilton, Cosmopolitan, Renaissance, and Marriott, along with projects for Disney and Tesla. The company also handles smaller runs, such as 25 to 50 countertop cosmetic testers.

The founders started with a vision of perfect craftsmanship and grew by teaching each new hire the same skills. The company emphasizes integrity, respect, community, teamwork, and safety as core values. Its differentiator lies in a one-stop-shop model that integrates design, engineering, prototyping, and finishing under one roof, all executed by experienced craftsmen rather than automated lines.

C&K Woodworks operates from a warehouse in Oak Park, Michigan, where founders Chris and Kai have spent roughly five years building a business around live-edge lumber and custom woodworking.

The shop produces custom tables, bar tops, countertops, and shelving, while also selling raw live-edge slabs for DIY builds. Customers range from homeowners furnishing a dining room to commercial clients outfitting offices and hospitality spaces. The warehouse doubles as a showroom where buyers can inspect slabs in person and consult on design details before production begins.

Chris and Kai emphasize a hands-on, educational approach—walking clients through wood species, finish options, and joinery choices—so that each piece reflects the buyer’s vision rather than a catalog standard.

name: CAS Cable
old_description: High speed internet and cable to keep everyone connected, plus local customer service you’ll love.
about:
CAS Cable operates from Parkersburg, West Virginia, where it has provided telecommunications services since 1977. The family-owned company traces its origins to that year, when the owner purchased a small antenna television system in Washington, West Virginia, selling over-the-air channels to customers within sight of the tower. The founder built the cable infrastructure himself, physically connecting a headend near the antenna tower to homes with coaxial cable.

Today the company delivers a triple-play bundle of high-speed internet, cable television, and digital phone service across Wood, Jackson, and Kanawha counties in West Virginia and parts of Washington County, Ohio. Residential plans range from 500 Mbps download with a 1.5 TB data allowance to a 3 Gbps tier offering 3.5 TB. Business customers receive dedicated internet and phone solutions, and the firm also streams local community events through its cable platform. Subscribers may lease a modem from CAS Cable or supply their own approved device, and a customer dashboard called MyCAS centralizes account management.

The service targets both households and businesses in the greater Parkersburg–Vienna area, Jackson County, the Charleston/Kanawha County region, and across the river into southern Ohio. Customers include remote workers, families streaming video, and commercial clients who rely on reliable voice and data connectivity for daily operations.

CAS Cable emphasizes its local, family-owned character as a differentiator: a live person answers every support call, technicians live in the communities they serve, and the company avoids automated phone menus. Its stated core values center on keeping services online around the clock, treating every interaction as a personal one, and restoring service quickly after storms or equipment failures.

Cambero Metal Works was founded in 2003 by Virginia and Angel Cambero in a garage in San Gabriel, California. Cambero serves industrial, commercial, and residential sectors, with specific experience in transit, rail, and government projects. Its client base includes architects, contractors, designers, restaurant owners, and kitchen designers throughout Southern California. Projects range from commercial kitchen equipment and ventilation systems to structural installations and ornamental metalwork.

The founders emphasize honest craftsmanship, personal attention, and a quality standard unchanged over two decades. The company states that its differentiator lies in treating each project with the same care as its own business, blending old-world craftsmanship with modern tools to deliver work that holds up long after completion.

name: Camgian
old_description: Camgian was founded in Starkville, Mississippi, establishing its roots in advanced technology and defense innovation.
about:
Camgian was founded in 2006 in Starkville, Mississippi, by Dr. Gary Butler, establishing its roots in advanced technology and defense innovation. The company began as a venture focused on artificial intelligence and machine learning for high-stakes environments.

Today, Camgian develops AI-enabled kill chain automation software, most notably its REACTOR® platform, which provides cognitive decision aids for air and missile defense, counter-unmanned aircraft systems, and space defense. The software is hardware- and command-and-control-agnostic, built on a modular, open architecture that leverages reinforcement learning, multi-modal sensor fusion, and real-time sensor cueing. The firm operates from its Mississippi headquarters and additional offices in Tuscaloosa and Lawton, Oklahoma, with a new facility opened in Huntsville, Alabama in 2025.

Camgian serves primarily U.S. Department of Defense organizations, including the Missile Defense Agency and the U.S. Army. In 2024 it secured a $55 million contract to support the Army's Integrated Air and Missile Defense systems, and it holds a position on the MDA's $151 billion SHIELD IDIQ contract vehicle. Its solutions are also offered to select non-DoD government entities and commercial partners.

The company states its mission is to accelerate decision-making in high-stakes environments by reducing cognitive overload and delivering precision at the point of decision. Its stated differentiators include platform-agnostic deployment, open-architecture scalability, and a culture rooted in radical accountability and a "No Quit" mindset.

about:
Caroba Plastics Inc is headquartered in Englewood, Colorado, in the Denver metropolitan area. The company was founded in 1983 by Barry Hart as a small, family-owned operation with two injection molding machines and a vision to provide high-quality plastic parts. Hart remains the owner and drives a hands-on philosophy emphasizing clean, organized facilities, systematic processes, and personal attention.

Today Caroba operates a fleet of 30 Nissei high-precision injection molding presses ranging from 20 to 750 tons, supported by in-house tooling design, maintenance, and repair. The facility includes an ISO Class 7 hard-wall cleanroom for medical molding and contract assembly, over 60,000 square feet of warehousing with lot and location control, and secondary operations such as assembly, packaging, and automated part removal. The company employs over 150 people and offers DFM assistance, mold validation, and ship-to-stock programs.

It holds certified "dock-to-stock" status for medical OEMs and semiconductor customers, and its quality system supports IQ/OQ/PQ validation, measurement system analysis, and process capability studies. The management team brings over 100 years of combined thermoplastic experience.

The company's differentiation stems from its founding principles: a clean, organized plant; systematic processes; honesty; and hard work. Project teams of engineers, toolmakers, and polymer experts engage from design inception to reduce errors and cost. Caroba has maintained ISO 9001:2015 certification since 1998 and operates with a "do it right the first time" attitude.

name: Carolina Precision Switchgear
old_description: Carolina Precision Switchgear specializes in refurbishing low and medium voltage circuit breakers restoring the equipment back to pristine condition.
about:
Carolina Precision Switchgear operates from Concord, North Carolina, in the Charlotte metropolitan area. The company was founded in 2006 by Doug Weaver, a former U.S. Navy interior communications specialist who spent 24 years as a nuclear supervisor at Duke Energy performing power-factor testing and circuit-breaker repair. Weaver launched the business to provide specialized refurbishing and testing services for low- and medium-voltage switchgear.

The firm’s core work is restoring circuit breakers to original performance through a full disassembly, cleaning, plating (silver or dichromate), repair, and reassembly process carried out by Level II PEARL‑certified technicians. A 10,000‑square‑foot facility houses calibrated test equipment including primary‑injection sets, while mobile trailers bring the same capabilities to customer sites. Through its affiliation with Group CBS, the company also offers engineering support, training, and access to over 800 CBS ArcSafe remote‑racking and remote‑switching products.

Customers span utilities, manufacturing plants, and commercial facilities. The shop services equipment from major manufacturers such as ABB, GE, Westinghouse/Eaton, Siemens, Square D, and Federal Pacific, as well as obsolete brands. Services range from preventive maintenance and infrared thermography to arc‑flash studies, high‑current testing, cable VLF/tan‑delta testing, and emergency troubleshooting.

The company emphasizes that reconditioning existing breakers can cost roughly 30 % of a new retrofill installation, saving customers tens of thousands of dollars. Carriage Hill Craft Metals operates from Georgetown, Massachusetts, on the North Shore. The company was founded in 2018 by Chris Breen, a Rowley native who graduated from Whittier Regional Vocational Technical High School in 2008 and spent the next decade honing his metal fabrication skills before launching his own shop. Breen formed the business as a limited liability company after acquiring Port Sheet Metal, a local firm with a 40-year service history.

The shop provides custom metal fabrication services including shearing, braking, punching, band-saw cutting, MIG and TIG welding, grinding, and soldering. Customers include residential, commercial, and architectural clients across the North Shore region, with projects such as a Newburyport railing installation exceeding 150 feet and a Corten steel deck on the Newburyport riverfront.

Breen started the business to apply his creativity and technical knowledge on his own terms, emphasizing the continuity of Port Sheet Metal's long-standing quality standards.

Cass County Electric Cooperative is headquartered in Fargo, North Dakota, and has operated as a member-owned electric cooperative since 1937.

It provides power to nearly 61,000 members, including residential, commercial, agricultural, and apartment accounts. Beyond delivery, the cooperative offers member services such as outage monitoring, bill payment, service start/stop/transfer, energy conservation programs, and safety education.

Its customer base includes residential urban and farm accounts, commercial businesses, irrigation operations, and lighting services. The cooperative also supports the broader community through programs like Operation Round Up, which funds local organizations, scholarships and youth programs, and partnerships with community events across its service area.

The cooperative distinguishes itself through its not-for-profit, member-governed structure. A locally elected board of directors sets policy, and the organization emphasizes safety, integrity, innovation, accountability, and community investment as core values. Profits are returned to members as capital credits, and decisions are made with long-term community benefit in mind.

name: City Hardwoods
old_description: In an industry filled with middlemen, our remote sawmill operation gives us the ability to supplement our wood room inventory with local hardwoods that have a unique story.
about:
City Hardwoods operates from Birmingham, Alabama, where it runs a sawmill, kiln-drying facility, and showroom The business was acquired in June 2022 by Caleb Gilbert, who runs the family-owned small business with his father. Gilbert’s path to woodworking began during his senior year at LSU when a shoulder injury sidelined him from baseball; he filled the time with weekend shop projects and soon shared the passion with his father, a lifelong hobbyist. Together they started milling and drying hardwood lumber for their own custom furniture projects.

The company’s remote sawmill salvages hundreds of urban logs each year from local tree services, diverting material that would otherwise become mulch. Logs are milled, stacked, and air-dried before finishing in one of two kilns—a dehumidification kiln and a vacuum kiln—that produce sterilized, kiln-dried lumber. Every board and slab is then surfaced on a planer or flattened on a slab CNC, a step that lets customers see grain, character, and color in the showroom. City Hardwoods builds custom furniture and retails the kiln-dried hardwood lumber, but does not offer milling or drying services to the public.

The primary customers are woodworkers, furniture buyers, and the broader Birmingham community seeking local hardwoods. The shop supplies lumber for custom furniture projects and sells boards directly to hobbyists and professionals through its retail showroom.

Gilbert says the operation was born from a desire to cut out middlemen and give each log a unique story. The dual-kiln setup ensures lumber is free of pests, and the slab CNC provides a showroom-ready surface that differentiates the buying experience. The acquisition of the existing City Hardwoods retailer in 2022 gave the family a platform to scale their sawmill output into a combined manufacturing and retail operation.

City Living Design highlights its construction methods as a differentiator—kiln-dried hardwood frames, sinuous coil springs, and high-density foam are cited for durability and ergonomic support. The firm also notes its Allied ASID membership, in-house design assistance, and the ability to deliver commercial-grade furniture for residential applications. Nationwide shipping and a collaborative quote process round out the service model.

old_description: Manufactures automotive batteries and energy storage systems (spun off from Johnson Controls).
about:
Clarios was founded in 2019 as a spin-off from Johnson Controls, establishing its headquarters in Glendale, Wisconsin. The company emerged as an independent entity focused on advanced battery manufacturing for the evolving transportation sector.

Today Clarios produces more than 150 million low-voltage batteries each year, employing roughly 7,000 people across a global footprint. Its product portfolio spans absorbent glass mat (AGM), lithium-ion, and supercapacitor technologies, as well as multi-battery architectures that integrate software, electronics, and AI-driven connected services. The company also develops recycled plastics for automotive applications and collaborates on sodium-ion battery industrialization.

The company serves four primary segments: automotive, commercial, powersports, and leisure. Its batteries power one in three vehicles worldwide, reaching customers in over 100 countries through brands such as LTH, MAC, Heliar, Delkor, VARTA, and OPTIMA. Customers include original equipment manufacturers and the aftermarket across passenger, heavy-duty, and recreational vehicles.

It differentiates itself through a chemistry-agnostic approach to low-voltage architectures, integrated electronics and software, and connected services that deliver actionable battery intelligence. Recent initiatives include expanding recycled plastics content and advancing sodium-ion technology with partners Altris and InoBat.

Its current 24,000‑square‑foot facility on 6.5 fenced acres includes 14 drive‑through bays equipped with welders, torches and a stand‑alone paint booth, and carries an inventory valued at over $750,000.

Customers span commercial, governmental and retail sectors across New Mexico and the broader Southwest. Notable accounts include the City of Albuquerque, Public Service Company of New Mexico, Kirtland Air Force Base, Navajo Utility Authority and various mining operations, alongside individual owner‑operators.

Clark Truck Equipment emphasizes its multi‑generational expertise, long‑tenured workforce (with employees marking 25‑ and 40‑year careers), and membership in the National Truck Equipment Association since 1967 as the foundation of its reputation for quality and personalized service.

name: ClassOne Technology
old_description: Electroplating and Wet Processing for Advanced Microelectronics
about:
ClassOne Technology is headquartered in Kalispell, Montana, where it designs and manufactures electroplating and wet‑processing equipment for advanced microelectronics. The company operates as ClassOne Technology Inc. and serves the semiconductor industry from its facility No founding year or founders are disclosed.

The company’s product line centers on the Solstice platform, offered in two configurations: the Solstice Max for 200 mm and 300 mm wafers (2–16 chambers) and the Solstice S‑Series for 3‑inch to 200 mm wafers (2–8 chambers). The equipment portfolio includes dedicated process chambers: the GoldPro™ Chamber, CopperMax™ Chamber, and Gen4 ECD Chamber for electroplating; a Wet Etch Chamber; and a Solvent & MLO Chamber for surface preparation. These chambers support a range of processes — copper TSV fill, copper RDL and pillar plating, multi‑metal stack pillars, advanced gold plating (including TWV, patterned, deplating, and fine‑feature fill), photoresist strip, metal lift‑off, UBM and patterned metal wet etch, RCA cleans (SC1/SC2), piranha (SPM), and emerging applications such as through‑glass vias, indium bump plating, and hybrid bonding.

ClassOne’s systems target advanced packaging houses, RF and sensor manufacturers, high‑reliability device makers, photonics and advanced‑sensor developers, and compound‑ and power‑semiconductor fabs. The company positions its tools for both production and R&D environments, emphasizing flexibility across a broad set of backend applications.

ClassOne states that its differentiator lies in removing “unnecessary complexity common to competitors” in favor of “more elegant and intuitive designs,” which it says yields faster recipe dial‑in, longer uptime, and lower operator and engineering burden. The platform is described as a common, easy‑to‑use, high‑performance foundation that maximizes performance relative to complexity and cost.

Cleaveland/Price Inc. traces its origins to 1975 in Trafford, Pennsylvania, when Chuck Cleaveland took on the responsibility of supplying renewal parts for discontinued Westinghouse switches. Today the company manufactures a full line of group-operated switches rated up to 345 kV, hookstick-operated switches, and motor operators. Its product portfolio also includes transmission-class in-line disconnect switches, solid-state motor operator controls, variable-speed motor operators, non-hydraulic operators for overhead switches, and automation controllers for retrofitting padmount and underground switchgear. Additional offerings encompass line sensors and data collectors such as the LineScope™ Power Quality Monitor, Reliatronics RTUs, and StayDry® corrosion-resistant bearing assemblies with hydrophobic membrane technology. Production takes place in a vertically integrated facility with extensive CNC machining capabilities.

Founder Chuck Cleaveland's stated goal of "no unhappy customers" underpins a quality policy emphasizing on-time, defect-free delivery and ethical dealings, with a certificate of registration available upon request.

Cleveland Yutaka Corporation operates in Shelby, North Carolina, as a subsidiary of Japan's Yutaka Industry Co., Ltd. The company was incorporated in June 1995 and completed its initial 56,788-square-foot facility in February 1996, launching production with 20 employees. A 2015 expansion added 52,552 square feet, bringing the plant to 109,340 square feet.

The shop specializes in high-volume, high-precision machined components using CNC machining, centerless grinding, and centered grinding. It holds diameter tolerances to 0.008 mm (8 µm) and surface finishes to 3.2 Rz, with standard capability targets above 3σ and special-characteristic targets above 4σ. Materials processed include aluminum, hardened and non-hardened steel, stainless steel, and cast iron. In-line and off-line visual and dimensional inspection, backed by proprietary and outsourced equipment, enables 100% nonconformity detection.

CYC serves the automotive sector, supplying components for fuel pumps, blower fans, starters, alternators, power-window drive shafts, solenoids, and suspension systems. Its customer base includes Toyota, Ford, General Motors, Chrysler, Hyundai, Honda, and other major OEMs.

The company states its goals as zero failed deliveries, zero late deliveries, and 100% quality. It emphasizes continuous improvement, employee development, and environmental responsibility through waste reduction, regulatory compliance, and safe chemical management.

name: Cold River Furniture
old_description: in 2019 and 2020 at the annual League of NH Craftsmen’s Fair, the oldest and largest craft show in the country.
about:
Cold River Furniture operates from South Acworth, New Hampshire, where master furniture maker Peter Maynard established his workshop in 1975 after completing an apprenticeship at the George Whitmore Furniture Company in Middletown, Connecticut. Maynard, who began his training at age 18 under second- and third-generation Connecticut River Valley craftsmen, moved to the upper Connecticut River Valley to start his own company. His wife, Marcie, has been integral to the business since its inception, handling communications and project coordination.

The studio produces original, handcrafted fine furniture using select North American hardwoods. Maynard combines antique water-powered machinery — including a 19th-century tenoning machine — with modern tools and extensive handwork. Joinery relies on full mortise-and-tenon and hand-cut dovetails, supplemented by Chinese and Japanese woodworking techniques. Each piece undergoes multiple sanding rounds, three coats of stain, and six coats of thin tung oil varnish. The workshop also handles log procurement, sawing flitch-matched lumber, and careful drying. Output is limited to signed, one-of-a-kind pieces shipped across North America.

Clients include private collectors, interior designers, and institutions such as the Metropolitan Museum of Art, which has commissioned work.

Maynard emphasizes a connection to the New England landscape and a commitment to integrity in craft. He describes the work as a deliberate alternative to mass production, where the mark of the human hand is central. The company's philosophy centers on creating heirloom pieces that gain value over time, rooted in a lifestyle of simplicity and focus.

about:
CoolCAD Electronics operates from Greenbelt, Maryland, where it designs and fabricates semiconductor devices and chips from wide-bandgap silicon carbide (SiC). The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm produces SiC MOSFETs, diodes, high-temperature integrated circuits, and deep-ultraviolet optical sensors. Its proprietary SiC formulations and manufacturing processes enable devices that operate continuously at temperatures exceeding 400 °C, well above the 200 °C limit of conventional silicon chips. CoolCAD also offers research and development services, computer-aided design and thermal simulation through its CoolSPICE software, cryogenic and radiation testing for space and nuclear applications, and engineering support for transitioning existing silicon-based power devices to SiC.

Customers span aerospace, automotive, data communications, green energy, military and defense, power generation, and water purification sectors. The company's high-temperature ICs and UV sensors are positioned for extreme-environment applications such as deep-space exploration, nuclear energy monitoring, and daylight UV imaging without optical filters.

CoolCAD holds multiple U.S. patents covering wide-bandgap SiC semiconductor advances. The technology was developed to accelerate the shift from fossil-fuel infrastructure toward renewable energy systems by delivering higher voltage, higher power, and smaller, lighter electronic systems.

about:
CorVent Medical, Inc. is based in Fargo, North Dakota, where it designs and manufactures critical care respiratory ventilation solutions. The company’s flagship product, the RESPOND® Ventilator, is developed and built in the United States to serve hospitals, long-term care facilities, government stockpiles, and rural health clinics. CorVent Medical emphasizes simplicity, safety, and smart technology to reduce complexity in critical care ventilation.

The RESPOND® Ventilator provides ICU-standard ventilation in a lightweight, portable platform. It supports invasive and non-invasive modes for patients from pediatrics (≥38 kg) through adults, with adjustable settings for flow triggering, oxygen concentration, and PEEP. Built-in safeguards include high inspiratory pressure, disconnect, and apnea alarms. The system operates with any low-flow oxygen source, uses multi-stage antiviral filters rated at 99.99% efficiency, and requires no proprietary circuits or high-pressure gas. A hot-swappable battery provides up to three hours of runtime, while nurse call ports and EMR connectivity enable remote monitoring and documentation. CorVent Medical backs the device with a five-year standard warranty and eliminates service and maintenance contracts.

The company serves acute care hospitals, critical access hospitals (CACs), long-term care hospitals (LTCHs), skilled nursing facilities (SNFs), and government stockpile managers. Its customer base includes respiratory therapy directors, chief nursing officers, ICU directors, and financial officers. CorVent Medical offers nationwide product demonstrations and evaluations to support procurement decisions.

The company holds ISO 13485 certification and complies with FDA 21 CFR 820.30 and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP). Its differentiators include a five-year warranty without service contracts, no proprietary consumables, and independence from high-pressure oxygen infrastructure.

name: Countryside Amish Furniture
about:
Countryside Amish Furniture operates from Arthur, Illinois, where owner Mel Stutzman purchased the business in 2010 after more than 25 years working in Amish furniture shops. Raised Amish with formal schooling ending at eighth grade, Stutzman progressed from sanding to finish room to shop foreman before moving into custom cabinetry. The company remains family-owned and operated, drawing on Stutzman’s direct experience to vet partner workshops.

The retailer offers made-to-order solid wood furniture across dining, office, bedroom, living room, nursery, and outdoor categories, with thousands of designs spanning Traditional, Farmhouse, Mission, Shaker, and Contemporary styles. Production is distributed among more than 100 family-run Amish workshops in Pennsylvania, Indiana, and Ohio. Customers select from North American hardwoods — oak, cherry, brown maple, tiger maple, walnut — and choose stains, fabrics, leathers, or Sunbrella outdoor textiles. Each piece is built with mortise-and-tenon, dovetail, and tongue-and-groove joinery, hand-sanded, and finished with catalyzed conversion varnish. Countryside coordinates the process, provides free material samples, and ships finished goods to the contiguous 48 states for a flat $150 fee that includes in-home placement and assembly.

Orders are split with half due at the shop and half at finishing, and lead times typically run 14 to 18 weeks.

Stutzman’s hands-on background drives the quality standards: he inspects hidden surfaces, requires solid hardwood for structural components, and insists on cut joinery that accommodates seasonal wood movement. The sales team maintains high-touch communication throughout the build, updating clients until delivery.

about:
Creative Werks Inc. was founded in 2003 by the Folkestad family in Des Moines, Iowa. The family-owned business began as an electronic engineering firm focused on RF and embedded controls for off-highway and utility vehicles, and has since expanded into a full-service design, engineering, and manufacturing operation.

The company designs, engineers, and produces a wide variety of electronic control systems entirely in-house at its Des Moines facility. Its capabilities span RF control systems, custom embedded electronics, electromechanical engineering, and wireless RF solutions. A full machine shop supports production with 5-axis and 3-axis CNC mills, dual-spindle lathes with bar feeders, and dual SMT pick-and-place machines for circuit board assembly. Creative Werks reports an annual output of roughly 65,000 systems, with capacity to double that volume. It also stocks off-the-shelf controllers — 4, 6, and 75-channel remotes, linear actuators, and basic control units — ready for immediate shipment.

Creative Werks serves off-highway, agricultural, industrial, mobile, and automotive markets, as well as prototyping and custom projects. Notable public projects include the Foxzilla vehicle build, the Josh Robinson tool cart, the Spool Rule, and wiring for Jeff Lutz’s 57-foot dragster. Customers range from OEMs needing custom embedded controls to aftermarket performance shops seeking PWM fan controllers and RF remote systems.

The company emphasizes total control over design, engineering, and production as its differentiator, maintaining quality through every step. Its combination of an engineering team and a fully equipped machine shop allows it to develop solutions that would otherwise require multiple vendors.

about:
Cristek Interconnects was founded in 1985 in Anaheim, California, by 23-year-old Cristi Cristich. Armed with a $25,000 contract from Litton, a fistful of credit cards, and a small loan from her first boss, she launched the company to serve the military and aerospace industries. Today, the business operates as a Qnnect Company with manufacturing facilities spanning Southern California, New England, and Northern Nevada.

The company designs and manufactures micro-miniature and nano-miniature connectors, complex cable and harness assemblies, twist capsules, precision mechanisms, hermetic assemblies, RF/microwave components, and machined parts. Its vertically integrated operation covers DC through 67 GHz RF frequency connector, cable, and electromechanical design and assembly. Cristek employs over 100 people across more than 56,000 square feet of production space.

Cristek serves aerospace, defense, and space programs, supplying prime contractors and other customers with mission-critical interconnects for harsh environments including vibration, temperature extremes, and vacuum. Its products are used in applications where failure is not an option, such as satellite constellations, laser communication terminals, and other high-reliability platforms.

Cristek differentiates itself through vertical integration, engineering expertise in nanominiature and microminiature connector technology, and the ability to add EMI filtering and hermetic sealing to custom high-speed, matched-impedance solutions. The company emphasizes process discipline, metric-based management, and rapid prototyping to accelerate development cycles while maintaining rigorous standards.

The company produces a wide range of dairy items including shredded, block, sliced, and snack cheeses, ricotta, specialty cheeses, cream cheese, butter, English muffins, and bagels. The brand also engages with community partners: it supports the national FFA organization and its Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Iowa chapters; donates products quarterly to the Ronald McDonald House; and supplies nearly all cheese and butter for All Square, a Minneapolis non‑profit grilled‑cheese shop that employs formerly incarcerated individuals.

The company says its Midwestern dairy heritage and a culture of commitment — from high‑quality ingredients to careful final inspection — are what set it apart, allowing customers to "cheese like a Midwesterner."

Custom Manufacturing Services, Inc. (CMS) and East River Metals, Inc. (ERM) operate from three facilities in Princeton, West Virginia, and Rocky Gap, Virginia. The business traces its roots to 1979 when Bob Graf founded East River Metals to produce metal enclosures for its sister company, American Mine Research. In 1995, Graf established Custom Manufacturing Services to combine ERM's sheet metal expertise with American Mine Research's electro-mechanical assembly capabilities.

The two entities together provide precision sheet metal fabrication, turnkey electro-mechanical assembly, and powder and wet spray coating. Core processes include laser cutting, forming, welding, hardware insertion, and outsourced plating. The combined footprint spans more than 155,000 square feet of manufacturing, office, and warehouse space across the two states.

Customers span mining, aerospace and defense, electronics, food processing, industrial machinery, and oil and gas. Named clients include American Mine Research, Moog, Pascor Atlantic, Forensic Computers, JBS, Caron, and Smyth Co. Machine.

The company emphasizes complete in-house control over fabrication, assembly, and finishing to deliver quick turnarounds and consistent quality. Custom Metal Products operates from Albuquerque, New Mexico, where it was established in 1988 after Steve and Cheryl Ryan purchased the business from a previous father‑son ownership. The Ryans built the company while Steve worked as a hotshot driver, and their son Keith later learned the trade before teaching Alan Cofran to run the operation in 1998. The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, cutting and bending mild steel from 29‑gauge to 16‑gauge and stainless steel up to 22‑gauge. A Berridge T‑panel machine adds radius‑forming capability for Berridge‑brand panels. The company also supplies sheet metal screws and clips and handles trim work in galvanized, copper and aluminum.

Its flexibility in accepting customer‑supplied material and its willingness to work early, late or weekend hours by arrangement make it a practical extension of a client’s own fabrication capacity.

The business was founded to give other companies a “metal shop” without the overhead of plant space, capital equipment, trained personnel or material inventory—a positioning it still emphasizes today.

about:
DC Equipment, Inc. was founded in 1995 and operates from its headquarters in Bethel Heights, Arkansas, with a 50,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Geraldine, Alabama.

The Alabama shop handles every stage of conveyor manufacturing, from raw steel to finished product. Certified welders perform TIG and MIG welding on stainless steel, carbon steel, and aluminum for frames and structural assemblies. A full-service machine shop runs CNC mills, manual lathes, and precision grinding equipment to produce custom shafts, sprockets, bushings, and one-off components. Additional capabilities include metal finishing (grinding, sanding, deburring, polishing), laser engraving for traceability, and final assembly with freight coordination. The company states it can handle projects ranging from single brackets to complete conveyor systems.

DC Equipment serves the poultry and food-processing industries, supplying processors with custom-engineered conveyance systems and a rapidly expanding parts division.
